descriptor: The largest wild dog, living and hunting in family packs across the forests, tundra and steppe of the north.

range.summary: Across much of North America, Europe and Asia, from Arctic tundra to deserts. Wolves are recolonising western Europe and parts of the United States after near extermination.
regions: Siberia and the Russian Far East

source.label: Wisconsin DNR, Annual Wolf Report 2026 and Gray Wolf Monitoring Report 2020

population.note: Counts from 1980 to 2020 are minimum late-winter counts from snow tracking and radio collars. The 2026 figure is a model-based estimate with a 95% credible interval, so it is not strictly comparable.

threats.title: Conflict over livestock
threats.detail: Attacks on sheep and cattle lead to legal culls and illegal retaliatory killing.

threats.title: Hunting and poaching
threats.detail: Wolves are hunted or trapped across much of their range, legally and illegally.

threats.title: Roads and fragmentation
threats.detail: Vehicle collisions are a leading cause of death for dispersing wolves in Europe.

threats.title: Hybridisation with dogs
threats.detail: Free-roaming dogs interbreed with wolves in parts of southern Europe and Asia.

places.name: Lamar Valley, Yellowstone National Park
places.note: Open valley where reintroduced packs are watched daily through spotting scopes.

places.name: Denali National Park
places.note: Wolves are sometimes seen from the park road in summer.

places.name: Algonquin Provincial Park
places.note: Famous public wolf howls on August evenings.

places.name: Sierra de la Culebra
places.note: Stronghold of the Iberian wolf with guided dawn watches.

places.name: Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise National Park
places.note: Apennine wolves that survived when the species vanished from most of western Europe.

sightings.tip: Winter is best in Yellowstone, when snow makes wolves easy to spot against open slopes and elk herds move to lower valleys. Algonquin's howls run in August.

actions.title: Support non-lethal livestock protection
actions.detail: Guardian dogs, electric fencing and night pens cut losses without killing wolves.

actions.title: Keep dogs vaccinated and under control
actions.detail: Loose dogs spread disease to wolves and can hybridise with them.

actions.title: Watch wolves ethically
actions.detail: Keep your distance, never feed wildlife and stay on roads and trails.

actions.title: Back wildlife crossings
actions.detail: Overpasses and underpasses on busy roads reduce collisions and reconnect populations.
